comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: 1 blocking, 3 important, 2 suggestion findings. The ladder/eviction core is well-built (stateless payload-only rewrite, bounded ladder, strong IT coverage — all 64 PR tests + neighboring suites green), but the new `ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent` has no wire-protocol encoder entry, so `encodeEvent` throws (`Null check operator used on a null value`) on any `fa serve`/SDK client at the exact moment the 413 ladder exhausts (verified by repro).

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 BLOCKING: `ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent` missing from `_eventEncoders`/`_eventKinds` (+ golden fixture, + TS `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS`) — crash on the recovery path (comment1).
- ⚠️ The AC6 gate checks the transcript instead of the refused payload: a strip-all-latched session re-runs the ladder (2 wasted sends + false recovery notes) on every later 413, verified by probe (comment2).
- ⚠️ Prominent drop notice names a cap and `images.maxPerRequest` for pass-2 evictions of current-message images — wrong cause, wrong knob (comment3).
- ⚠️ `ImageDropUx._latchKey` ignores the drop reason: cap→evicted transitions latch to silence (comment4).

**Next Steps**:
1. Add the wire encoder + kind mapping, golden fixture, and TS client kind; round-trip-test the failure event.
2. Gate the ladder on the refused request window (not the transcript).
3. Reason-aware prominent notice + reason-aware latch key in `image_drop_ux.dart`.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the AC6 gate checks the transcript, not the request payload — a latched session re-runs the ladder on every later 413**

`_needsImage413Recovery` gates on `_windowHasImages(context.messages)`, but `healIfNeeded` receives the loop's TRANSCRIPT context (`_streamAttempt` passes `context`, not the built `requestContext`). Because the rewrite is payload-only, the transcript keeps every image byte forever — so once the strip-all latch is set, the gate can never go false for a session that ever saw an image, and ANY later 413-class refusal (including a pure text-overflow one the comment says "belongs to the provider") re-engages the ladder.

Verified on this branch: strip-all latched + a well-formed image call/result in the transcript + an always-413 provider ⇒ **3 sends** (original + 2 ladder retries that cannot help — the payload is already image-free), 2 pass notices reading `recovered from 413: dropped 0, stripped N`, 2 false "recovered" notes injected as model-visible user messages, then the failure event + error. This repeats on every subsequent 413-shaped response for the rest of the session. IT-4's follow-up assertion ("latched image-free session … no ladder, no new failure notice") passes only because its follow-up history is text-only — a shape real post-image sessions never have.

Not blocking (bounded per response, the error still surfaces), but it contradicts the documented latch invariant ("later requests … cannot re-trigger the refusal") and burns 2 provider round-trips + emits misleading recovery copy per 413.

**Fix**: evaluate the gate against the request window that was actually refused — e.g. thread `requestContext` into `_finishedTurnResult`, or have `ImagePayloadRecoveryState` record whether the last build carried image bytes (`observeBuild` already sees the rewrite report) and stand the ladder down when the payload is image-free.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: pass-2 evictions of current-message images print the cap wording and the wrong knob**

`_noticeFor` branches on `currentDrops > 0` before the reason is consulted, so a strip-all eviction of the CURRENT message's images (`fromCurrentMessage: true`, `reason: ImageDropReason.evicted` — exactly what pass 2 produces) lands in the prominent cap branch. Verified on this branch:

```
prominent: true
line: 1 of 1 attached images were not sent to the model — cap is 20/request
      or ~8MB image budget; see /images or images.maxPerRequest
drops: (cur=true reason=ImageDropReason.evicted)
```

The PR's own principle for this enum is "an eviction names the cause … not a cap" (the history branch below does it right), but the prominent branch names a cap that never bound and points the user at `images.maxPerRequest`, the wrong knob — the remedy here is `images.maxBytesPerRequest` or a smaller-payload provider. Prominence itself is correct (just-attached images not sent is actionable); only the copy is wrong.

**Fix**: in the `currentDrops > 0` branch, partition by reason the way the history branch does — evicted current images get an eviction-worded prominent line (`N attached images replaced by placeholders (413 recovery) — lower images.maxBytesPerRequest or switch provider`).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the drop-notice latch is reason-blind — a cap→evicted transition is silenced**

`ImageDropUx._latchKey` (unchanged, just below) is `modelId|cap|current:<keys>|history:<keys>` — it does not include `ImageDropReason`. A set of keys that latched as byte/count drops in request N can become `evicted` in request N+1 (e.g. `/compact` after a byte-cap drop, or the 413 session latch) with the identical latch key, so `observe` returns null and the user never learns that those bytes now *never ride again* — a materially different situation per this layer's own contract ("a changed set … is exactly one updated notice"). The new mixed-line branch (`(+N evicted)`) only helps when the report's key changes for some other reason.

**Fix**: partition the latch key by reason, e.g. append `|evicted:<sorted evicted keys>` (or reset the latch when `evictedCount` transitions 0→>0), so the first eviction of an already-latched set still produces the one updated notice.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the armed recovery note can ride an unrelated later request**

`armNote` (called from `healIfNeeded` before the retry) is only ever consumed by the next request build via `consumeNote`. If the retry never happens — the user cancels, the run aborts, a steering resubmit is abandoned — the note stays armed and the NEXT build of the session (possibly minutes later, for an unrelated user message) rides the one-shot `[images] recovered from 413: …` user message and fires the host notice then, with no recovery immediately behind it. Counts stay accurate (refreshed by that build's rewrite), but the claim is stale.

Consider disarming the note when the streamed response ends without the retry consuming it (the response-local `_Image413RecoveryState` knows it armed it and can clear it on the exhaustion/abort paths).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: `dropped`/`stripped` on the loop-level event are dead fields, and the doc overpromises**

The doc here says "[dropped]/[stripped] carry the counts the rebuilt request rode", but the only emission in the entire PR is the exhaustion event with hardcoded `dropped: 0, stripped: 0` (`healIfNeeded`'s `passes >= 2` branch). Pass 1/2 surface through the host notice seam (`consumeNote`) only and never emit this event, so the wire kind `image_payload_recovery` can only ever carry a zeroed failure. Either emit the loop event on the pass retries with the real counts (IT-4's `recoveryLoopEvents` machinery is already in place to assert it), or trim the doc to "zeroed on the exhaustion event; per-pass counts ride the host notice seam" so the wire contract doesn't promise data it never carries.

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6xDC-V` — gate must evaluate the refused payload

Fixed, via the reviewer's second suggested mechanism (`ImagePayloadRecoveryState` records whether the last build carried image bytes).

- `rewriteRequestImages` now feeds the recovery state on EVERY build (`lib/src/agent/image_registry.dart:382`) — the #1889 image-free fast path included — via `observeBuild(..., carriedImages: payloadCariesImageBytes(rewritten))`. `payloadCariesImageBytes` (`image_registry.dart:394`) checks the REWRITTEN payload: riding `ImageContent` blocks plus current-message text-embedded `data:image/` payloads at the #1916 fold threshold (sub-threshold inline icons are legitimate text and never count).
- The gate (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop_image_recovery.dart:83`) evaluates `lastPayloadCariedImages && !stripAll` instead of the transcript — the transcript-shaped `_windowHasImages` check is deleted. A strip-all-latched session's payload is image-free, so a later 413 stands down: **1 send**, no pass notices, no false "recovered" notes, no failure event. The documented latch invariant ("later requests cannot re-trigger the refusal") now actually holds.
- In-flight exception: once a pass already ran for the streamed response (`passes > 0`), the ladder keeps ownership of its retry's refusal, so pass 2 and the ONE exhaustion event still fire (AC4) — otherwise the payload gate would have swallowed the exhaustion event on pass-2's own image-free retry.
- Tests: `image_recovery_loop_test.dart` IT-4b reproduces the reviewer's probe verbatim (strip-all latched + image call/result in transcript + always-413 ⇒ was 3 sends + 2 false notices, now 1 send, zero notices); IT-4c pins the text-only/icon shape; IT-4/IT-1 still assert the bounded ladder and the exhaustion event.

# Thread `PRRT_kwDOTXdlLc6xDDGq` — armed note riding an unrelated request

Fixed as suggested: the streamed-response wrapper disarms any note the ladder left armed when the response ends (`lib/src/agent/agent_loop_steering_yield.dart:386`).

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: the prominent eviction line can name the wrong cause**

`_noticeFor`'s evicted-current branch hardcodes the cause as `413 recovery`:

```dart
var evictedLine =
    '$currentEvicted of ${report.currentImageCount} attached images '
    'replaced by placeholders (413 recovery) — lower '
    'images.maxBytesPerRequest or switch provider';
```

Pass-2 strip evictions (`strip: true`) are indeed 413 recovery — correct. But a current-message image can also be evicted by the session-latched `evictedKeys` (`fromCurrent: true, strip: false`): a compaction boundary evicts a key, and later the same bytes are re-attached as the current image — the latch re-evicts it, and this prominent line blames 413 recovery. The `/images` surface gets this right by naming both causes (`image_drop_ux.dart:192`: `(evicted: compaction boundary / 413 recovery)`); the prominent line names only one.

Suggested wording: use the same both-causes phrasing, e.g. `replaced by placeholders (compaction boundary / 413 recovery) — lower images.maxBytesPerRequest or switch provider`. The remedy text stays as-is: for the compaction-latch cause the honest remedy is a new session (`/new`), but that's the pre-existing boundary-latch contract, and the byte-budget remedy is right for the dominant 413 shape.

Edge-case copy precision only; the notice still fires (the reason-aware latch key guarantees it) and never blocks.

The split is justified (the notice-seam type keeps `image_recovery.dart` — imported by `image_registry.dart` — free of the loop layer), but a short doc cross-reference on each class ("mirrors `ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent`; keep fields in sync") would keep the pairing from drifting. Optional polish.

comments.author: ai-teammate
comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: the ladder's failure event crashes every wire client — no encoder entry**

`ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent` is missing from `AgentWireProtocol`'s encoding tables. `encodeEvent` does `_eventEncoders[event.runtimeType]!(event)` and `_kindOf` does `_eventKinds[event.runtimeType]!` (`lib/src/wire/wire_protocol.dart:397-398`, `:1300`), and neither map has an entry for this event. Verified by repro on this branch:

```
AgentWireProtocol(version: 1)
    .encodeEvent(ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent(
        pass: 2, dropped: 0, stripped: 0, failed: true,
        providerError: 'error: 413: Request Entity Too Large'));
// → throws: Null check operator used on a null value
```

Blast radius: `WireServer.handleAgentEvent` calls `_sendSafely(_protocol.encodeEvent(event), client)` (`lib/src/wire/wire_serve.dart:310`) — the `encodeEvent` argument is evaluated OUTSIDE `_sendSafely`'s try/catch, so the throw propagates into the CLI's event pump (`_agent.subscribe(... server.handleAgentEvent(event))`, `agent_cli_wire_serve.dart:75`). The event is emitted EXACTLY on the ladder-exhaustion path (the AC4 "one actionable failure" moment, `healIfNeeded`'s `passes >= 2` branch), so for any `fa serve` / SDK / attach client the run breaks with an internal error at the precise moment this PR promises a clean, actionable failure.

Also missing for the new wire kind (the `task_ledger` precedent):
- golden fixture `test/wire/fixtures/v1/events/image_payload_recovery.json` (the conformance corpus pins "every live event kind"),
- `image_payload_recovery` in `KNOWN_EVENT_KINDS` (`sdk/web/src/wire-client.ts`) — today the TS client degrades it to unknown-passthrough.

Note the PR's own `test/wire/wire_adapter_test.dart` change only extends a test-local `_kindOf` switch — it never routes the event through `protocol.encodeEvent`, which is why this slipped through.

**Fix**: add `ImagePayloadRecoveryEvent` to `_eventKinds` (`'image_payload_recovery'`) and to `_eventEncoders` (`pass`, `dropped`, `stripped`, `failed`, `providerError`), add the golden fixture + the TS kind, and extend the wire round-trip test to encode the failure event.
